subject: Proposal: multi-year renewal with staged ramp and optional auto-renew opt-out
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@acmeindustries.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: multi-year renewal with staged ramp and optional auto-renew opt-out

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the great conversation yesterday. Based on your usage trends and growth plans, I put together a compact proposal to simplify renewals and give Acme predictable unit economics as you scale:

- 3-year term (May 2026–May 2029) with a staged ramp: 40% Year 1 / 60% Year 2 / 100% Year 3
- Option to opt out of auto-renew at the Year 2 review (60 days notice)
- Co-terming: we'll align the new term with your marketing analytics contract on 12/31/2026 to simplify invoicing (one invoice cadence)
- Billing: quarterly invoicing with an optional 10% prepay credit if prepaid annually
- Included: predictable SLA for latency and a 5% renewal discount for committing to the staged ramp

I've attached a one-page amendment (RDWD_Acme_Amendment_Proposal_v1.pdf) and a quick ramp table (Acme_MultiYear_Ramp_Table.xlsx) so you can share with procurement/finance.

If this framework looks reasonable, I can circulate an internal draft for legal and get pricing locked. Would you prefer we do a short call with procurement this week or should I send a tracked redline?

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Sofia —

Thank you, this is helpful and aligned with the direction we discussed. A couple quick items from our side:

1) Procurement would like to see an explicit escape clause for force majeure and a data residency confirmation for EU customers we integrate with later in 2027.
2) Finance will evaluate the prepay credit option; they may ask for Net-45 on quarterly billing unless we do the annual prepay.
3) We need to include Tim Lee (ops) on any SLA language that references latency guarantees.

I'll loop Tim in here. Procurement, please confirm if redlines or a call is preferable — we usually do an hour kickoff call for multi-year AMAs.

Thanks —

Hi Sara / Tim / Procurement —

Great notes, thank you. Quick responses and next steps:

- Data residency: Redwood can include a data residency clause restricting customer data storage to US or EU regions as required. We'll mark that for legal review.
- Force majeure: we'll include standard carve-outs; legal will provide the precise language in the amendment.
- Billing cadence & terms: if finance prefers Net-45 on quarterly invoices, we can accommodate but it will change the prepay credit economics slightly — I'll include both price lines in the draft.
- SLA: Marissa (AM) will take point on SLA wording and latency targets; Karthik (Sales Lead) is on scope/discount approvals.

Would Procurement be available for a 30–45 minute call tomorrow (Tue 5/11) at 10:00am PT to walk the amendment and confirm those points? If not, we'll send a tracked draft and ask for redlines by EOW.

Appended are the two attachments again for easy access.

Best,
Sofia

Hi team —

Adding a couple specifics from the AM side so you have clarity before the call:

- Latency SLA: 99.5% of inference requests < 350ms (p95) for the dedicated pool. For hosted tier we can set p95 targets per model class; we'll confirm for the models you're using.
- Year 2 review: we'll schedule a formal checkpoint 60 days before the Year 2 start to evaluate usage and allow the opt-out to be executed.
- Co-terming: to align to 12/31/2026 we propose a prorated first invoice that adjusts Year 1 consumption to match the 40% committed level across the shortened first period.

Procurement — if you want us to generate a tracked redline, we can send the first pass immediately after this call. Otherwise, I'm happy to be on the call tomorrow.
